thread:
infra-bot: :rotating_light: SLO ALERT: hosted-infer.gateway (usw2) p99 timeout spike detected. 502/504 fraction increased from 0.8% -> 6.7% in last 10m. Dashboard: https://console.redwood/slo/hosted-infer-usw2

maria: I’m seeing customer tickets from AcmeCorp complaining about 502s starting ~08:12 UTC. Paging @sam and @support-ops. Any quick triage steps?

sam: on it. initial hypothesis: prefetch/kv-cache TTL change in canary could be evicting entries too early and causing auth handshakes to fail -> 502s. Do we have auth error counts?

support-ops: Ticket #AC-12345 timeline: first reports 08:12. I pulled some logs — 502s peaked 08:13-08:22. No mass of 401s in customer logs but internal auth-proxy shows short-lived 401 burst at 08:11. Query I ran: ```logs.query("service:auth-proxy status:401 OR status:502 | rollup(count, 1m)")``` attaching raw snippet.

lee: Traces look weird — there’s a trace gap between ingress and runtime for many of the errored requests around 08:12. Sampling dropped for auth-proxy spans. Trace view: https://console.redwood/traces/trace?start=08:10&end=08:25

henry: Any recent deploys or config changes in usw2? Sampling or prefetch config flips?

sam: We started a canary at 07:50 UTC that changed `prefetch.max_ttl` from `30s` -> `5s` to reduce memory. Canary rollout target: 10% traffic in usw2. Deployment record: ```deploy apply --service hosted-infer --env usw2 --set prefetch.max_ttl=5s --canary=10% --id canary-2026-03-17-07-50```

maria: If that’s linked, can we rollback the TTL change? Support needs an ETA to share with AcmeCorp. Also any sign of billing hitting retries/duplicate charges due to retries?

support-ops: No 429s. Billing service shows a small increase in failed requests marked as retried around the same window, which could cause downstream accounting confusion. Correlation query: ```metrics.query("billing.failed_requests{service:hosted-infer} by {customer} | filter(timestamp >= 08:10 && timestamp <= 08:30)")```

lee: I can flip trace sampling to 100% for auth-proxy and gateway in usw2 for 15 minutes to capture full spans — doing that now and will post a link.

infra-bot: Deploybot: Rollback request submitted by sam — rolling prefetch.max_ttl back to 30s for canary group (change id: abc123). Started 08:36 UTC.

sam: Rollback complete at 08:41 UTC. Gradual traffic shift back to previous config; enabling debug kv-cache logs for 10m: ```env KVCACHE_LOG_LEVEL=debug duration=10m```. Monitoring p99 and 502 fraction.

maria: Great. Support-ops, please update AcmeCorp with rollback + monitoring note and ask for any request IDs still failing. @henry can you watch SLO and let us know when p99 drops to baseline?

henry: Watching. p99 trending down but still elevated on some request paths (multi-chunk streaming). I’ll return with a 30m update. If we still see 502s after rollback, we should check handshake TTLs between auth-proxy and runtime and also look for connection resets at the proxy layer.

support-ops: Updated AC-12345: rollback applied, monitoring in progress, will follow up in 30m and request request-ids from their side.

maria: Thanks. Follow-up action items: 1) sam — keep kv-cache debug logs for 10m and collect metrics, 2) lee — share full trace capture link, 3) henry — 30m SLO check and note any remaining tails.

sam: ACK. uploading kv-cache logs to /incidents/4532109876/logs and will attach summary.

lee: Trace capture link: https://console.redwood/traces/capture/4532109876?sampler=100%&duration=15m (captured auth-proxy missing spans, saving to incident).

henry: Noted. If customers still see errors after 30m, next step is to scale runtime pool and enable fallback variant for canary traffic.

maria: good plan. I’ll coordinate the customer comms.

(ends)
